description: WecOptTool is Sandia National Laboratories' Python toolbox for optimising wave-energy converter designs and controls. Its documentation describes constrained optimal-control studies, hydrodynamic response calculations and notebook tutorials. A modeller supplies a device representation, sea state, constraints and optimisation settings; the toolbox produces feasible control settings and estimated device performance for the chosen wave and time horizon. Geography is a selected offshore site or sea-state scenario, not a built-in national dataset. GPL-3.0 source and installation instructions are public through GitHub, PyPI or conda. A limitation is that hydrodynamic coefficients and operating constraints have to represent the actual device, and the current Python version differs from an older MATLAB implementation used in some publications. The model can support wave-generation capacity and control studies. The catalogue's model-openfoam offers a different fluid-dynamics method; no interoperability was tested. No package, geometry or example notebook was downloaded.
